description: No difference of typed-crossing words has counit epsNPq -- proved by a norm argument in Z[sqrt2] at the silver ratio. Side B (chi_block_*) confirmed symbolically.

data.bounded_sweep: m in [-14,14], c in [0,9]: 84100 pairs, 3 generic q -> 0 solutions for epsNPq, 1 solution for chi_block_3

verdict: EXCLUDED, scope-(b), by a proved invariant. eps of any typed-crossing word is q^m*([2]_q/2)^c. epsNPq carries the factor (q^2-2q-1), so it vanishes at the SILVER RATIO q = 1+sqrt2, where [2]_q/2 = sqrt2 exactly. A typed-word difference vanishing there forces (1+sqrt2)^(m1-m2) = (sqrt2)^(c2-c1); absolute norms in Z[sqrt2] (|N(1+sqrt2)|=1, |N(sqrt2)|=2) force c1=c2 then m1=m2, making the difference identically zero -- which epsNPq is not. So NO difference of typed-crossing words has counit epsNPq, and the corpus's description of Delta is inconsistent with its own asserted counit. Either the prose is wrong (Delta is not such a difference, and the real element is still unexhibited) or epsNPq is wrong (and with it Q_A and the ladder phase). NOT adjudicated here. The control confirms the argument does not prove too much: chi_block_3 IS such a difference and correctly survives. Excludes ONLY this class -- colour-weighted crossings fall outside the normal form, and A=1 nucleon words carry none.
